docs.text: Stratos / Wonder Valley, Box Elder County. Stage: Approved locally, state permits pending. Who decides: Military Installation Development Authority for land use; State Engineer for water; state agencies for air and water quality. Land use: Done. MIDA approved the project and the county consented to the project area. The governor said this decision covers land use only. A county moratorium does not apply because MIDA holds jurisdiction. Water right: Pending. Two earlier change applications (a54385 for 1,900 af; a54536 for 11 af) were withdrawn in May after thousands of protests. Protests do not carry over. A new application, a55167, was filed October 15; its protest window closed November 4. A hearing is the next step. Air permit: Not found. No application found. The state environmental quality commissioner said in May that air and water permitting were at least a year away. Water quality: Not found. No application found. Construction: Not found. No construction reported. Not found: Air and water-quality filings; hearing date for a55167; number of protests on a55167 (an advocacy newsletter reported 287 early on). docs.title: Basin view: ways to count data center demand
docs.text: Developer says: Counts only the annual water use each developer has published. Most projects have not published one, so this understates demand. Water rights: Counts the water rights each developer holds or is seeking. Per the research notes, unused rights can be sold or leased, so this can show risk the stated use does not. Highest on record: Counts the highest figure on record for each project, including independent estimates that account for on-site gas power plants. This is the cautious view. Engine estimate: uses the impact engine's central estimate for the current scenario, so a bill's levers move the basin scores.

docs.title: H.B. 76 (2026): Data Center Water Transparency Amendments
docs.text: H.B. 76 (2026), Data Center Water Transparency Amendments. Real measure. Status: Enacted; in effect July 1, 2026. Large data centers submit projected water use, discharge, treatment and reuse plans before construction. Those using 75 acre-feet or more a year report use and conservation efforts annually to the Division of Water Rights, which publishes the reports online. Data centers already operating or under construction on July 1, 2026 are exempt. The first actual-use numbers are expected around September 2027. Engine levers: reporting_threshold_af = 75. On the map: Reporting changes what the state knows, not water use: the map's water and lake estimates stay the same, and each project is marked as reporting or below the threshold. Not modeled: nothing further Basis: Summary of an agency presentation, not the bill text. (bill_id hb76_2026)
docs.source_name: Division of Water Rights presentation to the Natural Resources, Agriculture and Environment Interim Committee, Aug 19, 2026

docs.title: H.B. 60 (2026): Limits on factors in water-right decisions
docs.text: H.B. 60 (2026), Limits on factors in water-right decisions. Real measure. Status: Enacted; in effect May 6, 2026. Limits the factors the State Engineer can weigh when deciding water-right applications. Only the Legislature can change those limits. Engine levers: none (not modeled by the engine). docs.title: Research notes: USACE data available for Utah (first chat)
docs.text:
- **National Inventory of Dams**: `https://nid.sec.usace.army.mil/api/query?sy=@stateKey:UT`. Location, size, purpose, hazard, inspection, storage. Also an ArcGIS feature service.
- **National Structure Inventory**: building-level exposure data (GeoJSON by county or bbox; state GeoPackage).
- **National Levee Database**: levees.sec.usace.army.mil; sparse in Utah.
- **CWMS Data API**: time series, locations, ratings, forecasts; read without a key, filter office SPK; thin Utah coverage.
- **FUDS**: Utah SGID copy at `services1.arcgis.com/99lidPhWCzftIe9K/.../FUD/FeatureServer/0` (HIFLD Open was deactivated Aug 26, 2025).
- **RIBITS**: wetland mitigation banks and credits.
- **Gap**: no public API for Section 404 permits or jurisdictional determinations. Use public notices or FOIA.

docs.title: Research notes: Water use and new-demand risk views (second chat)
docs.text:
The use side comes from the Utah Division of Water Resources: M&I use, water-related land use, water budgets, and culinary supplier boundaries. Rights and distribution come from the Division of Water Rights: points of diversion, measurement stations, and the distribution network under prior appropriation. USACE supplies storage and exposure.
Five views: (1) current-use map by water system, (2) basin water budget, (3) storage and stress overlay (NID), (4) new-demand risk map (pending applications vs headroom, junior-right share, storage buffer, M&I trend), (5) scenario tester. Gaps: bulk pending applications, a 1–2 year lag in M&I data, growth projections (Kem C. Gardner Institute), and no 404 API.

docs.title: What this atlas is
docs.text: The Utah Environmental Atlas shows on a map how proposed data centers, and the bills that would regulate them, would affect Utah's water and the Great Salt Lake. It is decision support for the Legislature, not advocacy: it gives ranges from a sourced factor model, shows developer, engine and highest-on-record figures side by side, tags every published figure by source type, and makes no recommendations. Ask for a tour to be shown around (action start_tour).

docs.text: Layer 'Proposed data centers' (layer id atlas-projects). Each circle is a proposed data center; its area is the engine's central water estimate in acre-feet per year. Blue circles drain to the Great Salt Lake, brown ones to other basins. Click a circle for its estimate, the developer's stated use, water rights and the highest figure on record. Locations are approximate. To show one: select_projects and fly_to with its project_id.

docs.title: Impact tab: Legislation and the bill library
docs.text: Impact tab, Legislation sub-tab (impact_tab legislation). The bill library lists real measures (H.B. 76, H.B. 60, E.O. 2026-03, S.B. 132, Iron and Cache county moratoria) and mock bills. Applying a bill sets its levers and redraws the map (action apply_bill with a bill_id). You can also set levers by hand or paste bill text for Gemini to read into levers, each with its quote, confirmed before it applies.

docs.title: Map: with and without a bill
docs.text: When a bill or lever is applied, the map draws both cases at once: a dashed grey ring for each project built as planned (without the bill) and a solid ring for the scenario (with it), a dashed outline for the lakebed exposed without the bill and a filled band with it, and outlines for counties under a moratorium. A legend on the map gives the change in water use and lake level.

docs.title: Map: four branches strip
docs.text: The four-branch strip docks over the map for one project (action open_compare with a project_id). Its cards are Built as planned, Built with conditions, Delayed or scaled down, and Not built here. Choosing a card redraws the map for that branch. Rows below compare economics and environment with source tags; cells with no figure read 'Not quantified'. There is no net score. Not built here is not zero: relocation impacts are unknown.

docs.title: Impact tab: Basins
docs.text: Impact tab, Basins sub-tab (impact_tab basins) and layer 'Basin water risk' (layer id atlas-basinrisk). It scores each basin from counted demand against supply headroom, junior-right share, storage and growth trend, with a dry-year slider. The basin baselines are invented placeholders until the Division of Water Rights or Water Resources supplies data, so the scores show how levers shift relative risk and are not findings.

docs.title: Impact tab: Permits
docs.text: Impact tab, Permits sub-tab (impact_tab pipeline) and layer 'Data center permit pipeline' (layer id atlas-permits). Each project shows five gates: land use, water right, air permit, water quality and construction, with who decides, sources, dated events and open decisions. 'Not found' means no filing was found, not that none exists.

docs.title: Impact tab: Drop a project
docs.text: Impact tab, Drop a project sub-tab (impact_tab drop). Set a size in MW, cooling type, on-site gas and whether it drains to the Great Salt Lake, then click the map to place a hypothetical data center. The county is detected from the click and the engine adds it to the scenario.

docs.title: Impact tab: Who decides
docs.text: Impact tab, Who decides sub-tab (impact_tab context). Lists the audiences, the interim committees studying data centers, the legal context and the source-type tags.

docs.title: Map layers for water
docs.text: Layers tab, group 'Data centers & water'. Layer ids: atlas-projects (proposed data centers), atlas-permits (permit pipeline), atlas-lake (Great Salt Lake outline and extra exposed lakebed), atlas-basinrisk (basin water risk, placeholder baselines), atlas-water (computed water use by county), atlas-reference (county lines), atlas-wbd-tiles (USGS watershed boundaries), atlas-fema-tiles (FEMA flood zones). Use set_layer to turn one on or off.

docs.title: Great Salt Lake on the map
docs.text: Layer 'Great Salt Lake and extra exposed lakebed' (layer id atlas-lake). The tan band inside the lake outline has the area of lakebed the scenario would expose in the long run, counting only projects in basins that drain to the lake. The band has the estimated area but not the real shape, which follows the lake floor. To show it: fly_to place great_salt_lake.

docs.title: Legislative briefing
docs.text: The briefing (action open_briefing, or /briefing) is a one-page print view: statewide totals, what each lever would change alone, then by basin and by project, with a fixed data-limits box. It is watermarked as a draft while basin baselines are placeholders.

docs.title: Water screen for one proposal
docs.text: The water screen (/screen, or 'Screen' beside a project in the Impact tab and in a project's map popup) reviews a single data center proposal for a city council, county commission, water provider or state reviewer. It gives a first estimate of cooling water and power-plant water, checks the developer's stated water use against that estimate (too low, cooling only, partial or consistent), ranks ways to use less water, and lists red flags, questions to ask the developer, a scope for the in-depth hydrology study, possible conditions of approval and a screening memo to copy into a staff report. It opens with the facts the Atlas registry records for the project; what a developer has not disclosed stays unknown. The screen is a separate, simpler model than the impact engine: it uses national-average coefficients and counts water consumed by grid power plants, which the engine does not. Its claim check shows the developer's figure, the screen's estimate, the engine's estimate and the highest figure on record side by side, and never merges them. It is a screening estimate, not a hydrologic finding.

docs.title: Show the math and citations
docs.text: At the bottom of the Impact tab: 'Show the math' lists the formulas, factor ranges with sources and per-project assumptions. 'Copy citation' and 'Download citation' export the scenario's inputs, factors and sources as text for a filing or a memo.

docs.title: How to read the ranges
docs.text: Every engine output is a low, central and high value. Low uses every favourable input and high stacks every worst-case input, so the high end is an upper bound, not a forecast. Where a project has not said how it will be cooled or powered, the range spans the possibilities. Estimates are not measurements.

docs.title: Air quality and inversion tools
docs.text: The Today tab and the Conditions layers show live Utah DAQ air monitors, National Weather Service forecasts and the winter inversion estimate. The assistant can also answer from these live readings for wherever the map is centred.
